content:
Earlier this month, OpenAI launched its first GPT-6 model, paired with Astra. The GPT-6 series continues to expand with the official release of two new models: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are available starting today

According to the ChatGPT desktop app release notes, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna consume fewer tokens than their GPT-5.6 counterparts.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are rolling out on Codex and ChatGPT Work, with token pricing lower than the previous-generation GPT-5.6. Sol is suited to complex coding and agentic workflows, while Luna handles tasks that demand focus and high throughput. Both models will be phased in for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu users. Free and Go users can access Luna on the desktop app. Actual availability depends on rollout progress and workspace settings; Enterprise admins will need to enable the new models themselves. Inside ChatGPT, both models are available only on Work and Codex and are not yet on Chat.

Worth noting: there is no such thing as a GPT-6 Terra. It looks like OpenAI is gradually phasing out mid-tier sizes and keeping only three: Terra (small), Sol (large) and Astra (extra large).

Below is OpenAI's official announcement:

Even though the hardest, most consequential tasks still need the full depth of Astra, different jobs have different scales, paces and budgets. That's why we're extending the GPT-6 family with GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. GPT-6 Astra opened a new generation of intelligence, and these two models push the value even further, bringing those gains to a wider audience. We trained GPT-6 Sol and Luna using the same method we used for GPT-6 Astra, distilling Astra's leading capabilities in professional work, factual accuracy, coding, computer use and alignment into faster, more affordable models.

The company says both new models outperform GPT-5.6 and are priced below Astra (and the GPT-5.6 version it replaces). For example, the GPT-6 versions of Sol and Luna are priced 50% lower than the GPT-5.6 versions.
